atmospheric.greenhouse_effect: None (exosphere too sparse to trap heat)
atmospheric.weather_notes: No weather or winds; micrometeorite bombardment directly erodes surface.

environmental.radiation_level: Extremely High (Unshielded solar wind & coronal mass ejections)
environmental.water_or_ice: Water ice trapped in permanently shadowed polar craters
environmental.habitability_notes: Completely inhospitable to unshielded life; polar craters offer potential ice for ISRU.

Venus.name: Venus

atmospheric.magnetosphere: Induced ionospheric magnetosphere only (no intrinsic dipole)
atmospheric.weather_notes: Super-rotating hurricane-force cloud winds (360 km/h) with sulfuric acid rain evaporating before ground.

environmental.radiation_level: Low at surface due to thick atmosphere; High in upper atmosphere
environmental.surface_type: Basaltic volcanic plains, deformed tessera terrains
environmental.water_or_ice: No liquid water; atmospheric desiccated vapor (<0.002%)
environmental.geological_activity: Active volcanism evidenced by episodic SO₂ variations & young lava flows
environmental.habitability_notes: Surface is hellish; cloud layer at 50-65 km altitude offers Earth-like pressure (1 bar) & mild temps (20-60°C).

Venus.sources: NASA Venus Express / Magellan Mission Archives

atmospheric.magnetosphere: Strong intrinsic magnetic dipole (~31 µT at equator)
atmospheric.greenhouse_effect: Moderate natural greenhouse (+33°C warming, stabilizing liquid oceans)
atmospheric.weather_notes: Dynamic hydrological cycle, cyclonic storm systems, jet streams, precipitation.

environmental.radiation_level: Minimal; surface shielded by thick atmosphere & magnetosphere (0.007 mSv/day)
environmental.surface_type: 71% liquid water oceans, 29% continental granite & basalt
environmental.water_or_ice: Abundant liquid oceans, polar ice sheets, atmospheric vapor
environmental.geological_activity: Highly active plate tectonics, volcanism, earthquakes
environmental.habitability_notes: Optimal baseline for carbon-based life; self-sustaining biosphere.

atmospheric.magnetosphere: None; localized remnant crustal magnetic anomalies only
atmospheric.weather_notes: Vacuum; micrometeorite bombardment, solar wind sputtering, electrostatic dust levitation.

environmental.radiation_level: High (Cosmic rays & solar particle events: ~1.36 mSv/day, 200x Earth)
environmental.surface_type: Anorthositic highlands and basaltic maria covered in abrasive regolith
environmental.water_or_ice: Water ice detected in permanently shadowed craters at lunar poles (e.g., Shackleton)
environmental.geological_activity: Extremely weak deep moonquakes driven by Earth tidal stresses
environmental.habitability_notes: Prime target for Artemis base camps; polar ice deposits enable ISRU hydrogen/oxygen propellant generation.

Mars.name: Mars

atmospheric.magnetosphere: Remnant crustal magnetic fields; no global dipole
atmospheric.weather_notes: Planet-encircling dust storms, dust devils, cold CO₂ frost, high atmospheric winds.

environmental.radiation_level: High (~0.67 mSv/day, ~100x Earth background without shield)
environmental.surface_type: Iron-oxide rich silicate basalt regolith, ancient riverbeds, massive volcanic shields
environmental.water_or_ice: Vast water ice in polar ice caps & sub-surface permafrost; seasonal brine trickles
environmental.geological_activity: Low; occasional marsquakes detected by NASA InSight
environmental.habitability_notes: Most promising terrestrial candidate for human exploration; high ISRU potential via Sabatier fuel synthesis.

Mars.sources: NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter & Curiosity/Perseverance Telemetry

Phobos.name: Phobos

atmospheric.weather_notes: Direct solar exposure and Mars thermal re-radiation.

environmental.surface_type: Carbonaceous chondrite rubble pile covered in regolith
environmental.water_or_ice: Possible subsurface phyllosilicates or carbonaceous ice pockets
environmental.geological_activity: Inactive; decaying orbit experiencing tidal disruption in ~40 Myr
environmental.habitability_notes: Ideal low delta-v staging base and communications relay for Mars exploration.

Phobos.sources: ESA Mars Express & NASA MAVEN Science Team

Ceres.name: Ceres

atmospheric.weather_notes: Sublimation transient plumes triggered by solar perihelion.

environmental.radiation_level: High interplanetary galactic cosmic ray exposure
environmental.surface_type: Hydrated clays, sodium carbonate salts (Occator Crater faculae)
environmental.water_or_ice: Enormous water ice mantle (up to 25% of total mass is water/ice)
environmental.habitability_notes: Water-rich oasis of the Asteroid Belt; primary candidate for in-space water harvesting.

Ceres.sources: NASA Dawn Mission Results (JPL/Dawn Science Team)

Jupiter.name: Jupiter

atmospheric.pressure_display: 100+ bar (Continuous fluid transition, no solid surface)
atmospheric.magnetosphere: Vast, strongest in Solar System (20,000x Earth magnetic moment)
atmospheric.greenhouse_effect: Significant internal heat generation (radiates 1.6x energy absorbed)
atmospheric.weather_notes: Anticyclonic storms (Great Red Spot), Zonal jet streams up to 540 km/h, ammonia lightning.

environmental.radiation_level: Extreme lethal radiation belts trapped in Jovian magnetosphere (up to 500 Sv/day in core belts)
environmental.surface_type: No solid surface; supercritical hydrogen fluid ocean grading into metallic hydrogen
environmental.water_or_ice: Atmospheric water vapor detected by Juno probe (~0.25% deep atmosphere)
environmental.geological_activity: Atmospheric vortex dynamics and metallic hydrogen dynamo
environmental.habitability_notes: Uninhabitable for landers; atmosphere probes viable with massive titanium heat shields.

Jupiter.sources: NASA Juno Mission Science & Galileo Atmospheric Probe

Io.name: Io

atmospheric.magnetosphere: None; generates an intense electrical flux tube coupling to Jupiter
atmospheric.weather_notes: Volcanic SO₂ frost plumes erupting up to 500 km above surface; collapses in Jupiter shadow.

environmental.radiation_level: Deadly Jovian radiation belt exposure (~36 Sv/day; human lethal dose in minutes)
environmental.surface_type: Ultramafic silicate lava lakes, sulfur frost, and active calderas
environmental.water_or_ice: Extremely desiccated; virtually zero water detected
environmental.geological_activity: Most volcanically active body in the Solar System (tidal flexing by Jupiter & Europa)
environmental.habitability_notes: Lethal radiation and extreme volcanism make surface survival nearly impossible.

Io.sources: NASA Galileo, New Horizons & Juno Spacecraft Imagery

Europa.name: Europa

atmospheric.magnetosphere: Induced magnetic field confirming a conductive subsurface liquid saltwater ocean
atmospheric.weather_notes: Surface sputtering by Jovian magnetospheric ions; water vapor geysers venting into space.

environmental.radiation_level: Extremely High (~5.4 Sv/day on surface from trapped Jovian electrons)
environmental.surface_type: Smooth water-ice shell (15-25 km thick) crisscrossed by reddish lineae fractures
environmental.water_or_ice: Subsurface liquid saltwater ocean containing 2-3x all Earth's oceans combined
environmental.geological_activity: Ice tectonics, chaos terrain, hydrothermal vents on deep ocean floor
environmental.habitability_notes: Prime candidate for extraterrestrial life in warm, chemically rich sub-ice ocean.

Europa.sources: NASA Europa Clipper Mission Database & Galileo Telemetry

Ganymede.name: Ganymede

atmospheric.magnetosphere: Intrinsic magnetic dipole (only moon in Solar System with one; ~719 nT)
atmospheric.weather_notes: Auroral belts around polar regions driven by magnetosphere interactions.

environmental.radiation_level: Moderate-High (~0.08 Sv/day; shielded partially by internal magnetic field)
environmental.surface_type: Dark ancient cratered terrain and light younger grooved tectonic terrain
environmental.water_or_ice: Sandwiched subsurface liquid ocean beneath ~100 km ice shell
environmental.geological_activity: Ancient extensional tectonics; weak current convective ice motion
environmental.habitability_notes: Largest moon in Solar System (bigger than Mercury); intrinsic magnetosphere shields explorers.

Ganymede.sources: ESA JUICE Science Planning & NASA Juno Flyby (2021)

atmospheric.magnetosphere: Weak induced magnetic field indicative of salty subsurface liquid
atmospheric.weather_notes: No weather; sublimating carbon dioxide frost.

environmental.radiation_level: Low (~0.01 mSv/day; sits outside Jupiter's main radiation belts)
environmental.surface_type: Most heavily cratered surface in Solar System; mixed ice and dark rock
environmental.water_or_ice: Deep ocean possibly beneath ~150-200 km thick mixed ice/rock crust
environmental.geological_activity: Geologically dead; no tidal heating resonance
environmental.habitability_notes: Safest location in the Jovian system for human base staging due to negligible radiation.

atmospheric.magnetosphere: Symmetric dipolar magnetosphere aligned almost perfectly with rotation axis (<0.01°)
atmospheric.greenhouse_effect: High internal heat emission (generates 2.5x energy received from Sun)
atmospheric.weather_notes: Supersonic equatorial jet winds (up to 1,800 km/h); giant Hexagon storm at north pole.

environmental.radiation_level: Moderate-High radiation belts absorption moderated by ring particles
environmental.surface_type: No solid surface; density lower than water (0.687 g/cm³)
environmental.water_or_ice: Spectacular ring system composed of 99% pure water ice particles
environmental.geological_activity: Atmospheric convective storms and helium rain segregation
environmental.habitability_notes: Inhabitable directly; rings and 146 moons offer limitless volatile resource potential.

Titan.name: Titan

atmospheric.magnetosphere: None; shielded by Saturn's magnetosphere most of orbit
atmospheric.greenhouse_effect: Anti-greenhouse organic haze cools surface, but methane provides mild greenhouse (+21K)
atmospheric.weather_notes: Full hydrological cycle with liquid methane/ethane clouds, rainfall, rivers, and polar seas.

environmental.radiation_level: Extremely Low on surface (thick atmosphere absorbs GCRs and solar wind)
environmental.surface_type: Solid water-ice bedrock coated in complex tholin organic dunes and liquid hydrocarbon lakes
environmental.water_or_ice: Global liquid methane/ethane seas (Kraken Mare) and deep subsurface water-ammonia ocean
environmental.geological_activity: Cryovolcanism, wind erosion, methane rain river valleys
environmental.habitability_notes: Only moon with dense atmosphere; humans would only need warm thermal suit & oxygen mask (no pressure suit needed!).

Titan.sources: Cassini Radar & ESA Huygens Probe In-situ Measurements

Enceladus.name: Enceladus

atmospheric.magnetosphere: Perturbs Saturn's magnetosphere via E-ring plasma feeding
atmospheric.weather_notes: Continuous supersonic cryovolcanic plumes shooting vapor & ice 500 km into orbit.

environmental.radiation_level: Low-Moderate; shielded inside Saturn's protective magnetosphere bubble
environmental.surface_type: Fresh pristine water ice (highest albedo in Solar System: 0.99); tiger stripe thermal fractures
environmental.water_or_ice: Global subsurface liquid water ocean with alkaline pH (9-11) & silica nanoparticles
environmental.geological_activity: Active cryovolcanism powered by tidal dissipation from orbital resonance with Dione
environmental.habitability_notes: Possesses all three keystones for life: liquid water, organic carbon molecules, and hydrothermal energy.

Enceladus.sources: NASA Cassini Cosmic Dust Analyzer & INMS Plume Flythroughs

Uranus.name: Uranus

atmospheric.magnetosphere: Tilted corkscrew magnetosphere (59° off rotational axis, displaced 1/3 radius)
atmospheric.greenhouse_effect: Uniquely low internal heat emission compared to other giants
atmospheric.weather_notes: Extreme seasonal atmospheric swings due to rolling-ball 98° axial tilt; methane clouds & storms.

environmental.radiation_level: Moderate trapped radiation belts in twisted magnetosphere
environmental.surface_type: No solid surface; dense supercritical water, ammonia, and methane ice mantle
environmental.water_or_ice: Enormous volatile ice reservoir (~65% of planetary mass is water/ammonia/methane 'ices')
environmental.geological_activity: Internal convective transport and diamond precipitation potential
environmental.habitability_notes: Harsh cryogenic deep space destination; prime target for future orbiter atmospheric probes.

Uranus.sources: NASA Voyager 2 Data & Hubble / JWST Spectroscopy

Neptune.name: Neptune

atmospheric.magnetosphere: Tilted offset magnetosphere (47° tilt, offset by 0.55 radii from core)
atmospheric.greenhouse_effect: Vigorous internal heat source (radiates 2.6x energy absorbed from faint Sun)
atmospheric.weather_notes: Fastest winds in Solar System reaching 2,100 km/h; dynamic Great Dark Spot storms.

environmental.surface_type: No solid surface; high-pressure liquid mantle of water, methane, and ammonia
environmental.water_or_ice: Dense fluid ionic water ocean under megabar pressures surrounding small silicate core
environmental.habitability_notes: Outermost major planet; requires nuclear propulsion (RTG/Fission) due to solar flux <0.1% Earth.

Neptune.sources: NASA Voyager 2 Data & JWST NIRCam Observations (2022-2024)

Triton.name: Triton

atmospheric.magnetosphere: None; embedded inside Neptune's eccentric magnetosphere
atmospheric.weather_notes: High nitrogen ice clouds and wind streaks driven by subsurface sublimation.

environmental.surface_type: Cantaloupe terrain made of diapiric nitrogen, water, and methane ice crust
environmental.water_or_ice: Solid frozen nitrogen surface covering deep water-ice crust and probable subsurface ocean
environmental.geological_activity: Active nitrogen cryogeysers erupting up to 8 km high carrying dark organic tholins
environmental.habitability_notes: Captured Kuiper Belt Object in retrograde orbit; tidal dissipation maintains potential interior ocean.

Triton.sources: Voyager 2 Flyby Analysis & New Horizons Outer Solar System Studies

Pluto.name: Pluto

atmospheric.greenhouse_effect: Anti-greenhouse methane effect cooling the upper atmosphere
atmospheric.weather_notes: Seasonal atmospheric freezing: atmosphere slowly collapses onto surface as Pluto moves toward aphelion.

environmental.surface_type: Nitrogen-ice glaciers (Sputnik Planitia), water-ice mountains rising 3,500m, tholin stains
environmental.water_or_ice: Vast nitrogen/carbon monoxide ice fields and liquid water-ammonia ocean beneath Sputnik Planitia
environmental.geological_activity: Active cellular ice convection and cryovolcanic domes (Wright Mons, Piccard Mons)
environmental.habitability_notes: Complex geologically youthful world with subsurface ocean despite receiving 1/1600th Earth solar flux.

Pluto.sources: NASA New Horizons Science Team (2015-2023 Published Catalogs)
